heroHeadline: Pacific Gray Whale Population Halved in a Decade; BC First Nations Sign Historic Marine Conservation Area as Mombasa Ocean Conference Approaches
heroSubtitle: A major investigation published May 24, 2026 revealed the eastern Pacific gray whale population has been cut in half over the past decade — from approximately 27,000 individuals in 2016 to roughly 13,000 today — as 22 emaciated carcasses washed ashore along Washington State's coast this spring. Scientists at Cascadia Research Collective link the collapse to Arctic sea ice loss destroying the benthic food chain, with calf births dropping ~95%. On May 22, six BC First Nations (Wuikinuxv, Nuxalk, Kitasoo Xai'xais, Heiltsuk, Gitxaała, and Gitga'at) and Canada signed the 'Mia-yaltwa Ha'lidzogm hoon' (Realm of the Salmon) dual marine protected area — the first in Canada to simultaneously hold National Marine Conservation Area Reserve and Indigenous Protected and Conserved Area status with the same footprint. With the Our Ocean Conference scheduled for Mombasa, Kenya on June 16–18, and J.P. Morgan valuing the global gross marine product at $2.5 trillion annually, ocean-climate alarm and conservation finance are converging toward what may be a critical pledging moment for ocean protection.
